data_source_notes: STEP 1 (primary): The documented endpoint path https://api.ransomware.live/v2/victims/sector/Healthcare returned HTTP 302 redirects to /apidocs/ (i.e., did not exist as documented). Probing found the correct working endpoint is https://api.ransomware.live/v2/sectorvictims/Healthcare (no slash-delimited path), which returned HTTP 200 with the full victim list. First call hit the "1 per 1 minute" rate limit; a retry after ~65+ seconds (during which Step 2/3 work was performed) succeeded and returned 2,443 victim records covering 2015-07-19/20-2026. All aggregate stats and group/country/year breakdowns in this report were computed directly from that raw JSON dataset. STEP 2 (supplementary, both failed/unavailable, as anticipated as an acceptable outcome by the task instructions): ransomlook.io's documented search endpoint (/api/search) returned HTTP 400/404 for multiple query formats tried (query param and path param); ransomwhat.telemetry.ltd/posts.json 302-redirected to ransomwatch.telemetry.ltd, and the direct posts.json path on that host returned HTTP 404 (the API surface appears to have changed/moved). No corroborating data was obtained from either supplementary source; this does not affect confidence in the primary dataset, which was successfully retrieved directly. Individual incident financial/impact figures in example_incidents were sourced via WebSearch against news outlets, HIPAA Journal, SEC filings, and official NHS/government statements; where a specific figure was not found in available reporting, this is explicitly noted as "not publicly disclosed" rather than estimated.

overview: The Information Technology sector (software vendors, IT-services/MSPs, SaaS/cloud hosts, distributors, semiconductor/EDA and telecom-adjacent firms) is one of the two most-targeted industries in ransomware, consistently ranking behind only manufacturing. Its defining risk feature is systemic/aggregation exposure: IT companies sit upstream of thousands of downstream customers, so a single intrusion into an MSP platform (Kaseya), a managed file-transfer product (MOVEit/Progress), a SaaS provider (CDK Global), or a distributor (Ingram Micro) cascades into mass downstream outages and data loss far larger than the direct victim. Beyond encryption-based extortion, the sector is disproportionately exposed to data-theft/leak extortion and intellectual-property theft (source code, chip designs, product blueprints). Common initial-access paths are the sector's own internet-facing edge (VPNs, RMM tools, MFT appliances), leaked/infostealer credentials, and exploitation of vulnerabilities in products the companies themselves ship. Regulatory exposure is intensifying (SEC cyber-disclosure rules, GDPR, breach-notification statutes, and large class-action liability). Sector-level economics per Sophos 2025 and IBM 2025: technology accounts for roughly 9% of ransomware incidents; the average technology-sector data-breach cost is about $4.79M, and the average ransomware/extortion incident costs about $5.08M.

hazard_categories.description: How ransomware operators break into IT-sector firms. The sector's large internet-facing attack surface (the very appliances and products it builds and operates) makes edge exploitation and credential abuse dominant.
subcategories: Exploitation of internet-facing/VPN and edge appliances (e.g., Palo Alto GlobalProtect at Ingram Micro, Fortinet/Citrix, Microsoft Exchange as used against Acer)
Exploitation of managed file transfer / edge software (MOVEit, GoAnywhere, Accellion) for mass exfiltration
Leaked or purchased credentials and infostealer logs (initial-access-broker marketplaces)
Abuse of remote monitoring & management (RMM) and remote-access tooling
Phishing / social engineering of admins and developers
Exploitation of zero-day/n-day vulnerabilities in the vendor's own shipped products, turning the product into an attack vector against customers

hazard_categories.description: IT firms face the full multi-extortion playbook; data-theft and source-code/IP leak threats are especially potent because reputation and confidentiality are core to the business.
subcategories: Encryption of production, build/CI-CD and virtualization (VMware ESXi) systems
Data exfiltration and public leak-site publication (double extortion)
Triple/quadruple extortion: DDoS and direct harassment of the victim's downstream customers, partners and employees
Threatened disclosure of source code, product blueprints and signing keys/certificates
Ransom escalation and event-timed pressure (e.g., REvil publicizing Quanta/Apple leak during Apple's launch event)

hazard_categories.description: The signature hazard of the IT industry: because these firms are technology suppliers, a single compromise propagates to their entire customer base, creating catastrophic aggregation/accumulation risk for insurers.
subcategories: MSP/RMM platform compromise cascading to managed clients (Kaseya VSA -> up to ~1,500 downstream businesses)
SaaS/hosted-platform outage cascading to customer operations (CDK Global -> ~15,000 dealerships)
Distribution/reseller channel disruption halting downstream commerce (Ingram Micro order processing)
Software-supply-chain / trojanized-update or embedded-product-vulnerability propagation (MOVEit -> 2,700+ organizations)
Cloud/subprocessor concentration and single-points-of-failure shared across many tenants

hazard_categories.category: Intellectual Property and Source Code Theft
hazard_categories.description: IT firms hold uniquely high-value technical IP whose theft is itself the extortion leverage, independent of encryption.
subcategories: Product designs and hardware blueprints (Quanta/Apple device schematics)
Semiconductor / chip design and EDA data (ARM, Synopsys as recent leak-site claims)
Proprietary source code and algorithms
Code-signing keys, certificates and secrets enabling further supply-chain abuse
Trade secrets, roadmaps and confidential customer contracts

hazard_categories.description: Dependence on shared infrastructure and a dense web of subprocessors amplifies both the likelihood and blast radius of incidents.
subcategories: Shared cloud/hosting infrastructure and multi-tenant architecture
Subprocessor and nested-vendor dependency chains
Data-processor liability for downstream clients' data held on behalf of customers
Concentration of many customers on one platform (systemic insurer accumulation risk)

hazard_categories.description: IT breaches trigger outsized legal and disclosure consequences given the volume of third-party data and public-company status of many victims.
subcategories: SEC cyber-incident disclosure obligations and investigations (SEC probe of Progress Software/MOVEit)
GDPR and global breach-notification statutes across many jurisdictions
Mass class-action litigation (MOVEit spawned dozens of suits, 40M+ claimants)
Contractual SLA penalties, indemnities and customer breach-of-contract claims
Cross-border data-transfer and sovereignty complications

hazard_categories.description: IT staff hold the keys to both their own and customers' environments, making identity compromise and privileged-access abuse especially damaging.
subcategories: Compromise of privileged admin / domain-admin and cloud root credentials
Developer credential and secrets theft (repo tokens, API keys)
Initial-access-broker recruitment and insider collusion
Weak MFA / SSO federation abuse across tenants

hazard_categories.description: For the IT sector the critical 'operational technology' is the data center, network and cloud fabric; loss of availability is the primary business-interruption driver rather than physical production lines.
subcategories: Data-center / colocation and network-operations disruption
Backup and disaster-recovery system targeting (attackers delete/encrypt backups first)
Virtualization and hypervisor mass-encryption (ESXi)
Prolonged availability loss and business-interruption for both victim and downstream customers

exposure_categories.description: The crown-jewel assets unique to technology firms; their exposure enables both direct IP loss and downstream supply-chain compromise.
subcategories: Source-code repositories (Git/GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket)
CI/CD build and release pipelines
Code-signing keys and certificates
Container registries and artifact stores
Product designs, hardware blueprints and chip/EDA design data

exposure_categories.description: The revenue-generating production systems whose downtime directly halts thousands of customers.
subcategories: Production application and hosting environments
Multi-tenant customer databases and data lakes
Customer portals, dashboards and public APIs
Licensing, provisioning and entitlement systems

exposure_categories.description: Tooling that grants privileged reach into customer estates, making it a high-value pivot for cascade attacks.
subcategories: RMM platforms (e.g., Kaseya VSA)
MSP management consoles and multi-tenant admin planes
Remote-access/jump hosts and privileged-access management
Monitoring, patching and orchestration tooling

exposure_categories.category: Corporate IT, Identity and Edge Systems
exposure_categories.description: The internal backbone whose compromise enables lateral movement and encryption.
subcategories: Active Directory / Entra ID and SSO/identity federation
VPN and internet-facing edge appliances (GlobalProtect, Fortinet, Citrix)
Managed file transfer appliances (MOVEit, GoAnywhere)
Virtualization (VMware ESXi), email and collaboration systems
Backup and disaster-recovery infrastructure

exposure_categories.description: IT firms hold vast volumes of both their own and their customers' data as processors, magnifying breach-notification and liability exposure.
subcategories: Customer PII and account credentials
Contract, service-order and billing data (e.g., NTT Com 17,891 organizations)
Employee and applicant records (e.g., Ingram Micro ~42,000 records)
Downstream clients' data held as a data processor
Confidential customer contracts, purchase orders and roadmaps (Tata Technologies leak)

exposure_categories.description: For IT distributors/resellers and platform providers, transactional systems are the business; their loss stops downstream commerce.
subcategories: Order-processing and e-commerce systems (Ingram Micro)
ERP, inventory and channel-management platforms
Dealer/reseller management SaaS (CDK Global DMS)
Payment and licensing/activation systems

exposure_categories.description: The third parties whose exposure flows through the IT firm, creating aggregation risk.
subcategories: MSP-managed client estates
Reseller/distributor channel and end customers
Subprocessors, cloud providers and integration partners
Hardware and component supply chain (OEM/ODM relationships, e.g., Quanta as Apple ODM)

exposure_categories.description: High-value proprietary knowledge whose exfiltration is itself the extortion leverage.
subcategories: Semiconductor and chip-design IP / EDA data
Proprietary algorithms, models and product roadmaps
Unreleased product blueprints and schematics
Trade secrets and competitive/strategic documents

example_incidents.summary: REvil exploited zero-day vulnerabilities in Kaseya's VSA remote-monitoring-and-management software to push ransomware through ~60 direct MSP customers to their downstream clients — the archetypal IT supply-chain cascade attack.
example_incidents.financial_impact: Direct financial loss to Kaseya not publicly disclosed; downstream impact spanned 800-1,500 businesses across ~17 countries (e.g., Sweden's Coop grocery chain closed ~800 stores). Broader economic cost not authoritatively quantified.
example_incidents.ransom_demanded_or_paid: REvil demanded a single universal-decryptor payment of $70 million in Bitcoin. Kaseya states it did NOT pay the ransom; it obtained a universal decryptor from a 'trusted third party' (later reported as provided via the FBI).
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: VSA SaaS and on-prem servers taken offline as a precaution on July 2; patched VSA restored around July 11-12; a universal decryptor was distributed on July 22-23, 2021 to help victims restore data. Recovery for downstream MSP clients ran days to weeks.
example_incidents.data_impact: Primarily encryption/availability impact rather than mass data theft; up to ~1,500 downstream organizations had systems encrypted.

example_incidents.summary: Clop mass-exploited a zero-day SQL-injection flaw (CVE-2023-34362) in Progress Software's MOVEit managed-file-transfer product to steal data from thousands of organizations worldwide — one of the largest supply-chain data-extortion campaigns on record.
example_incidents.financial_impact: Aggregate downstream cost estimated by Emsisoft at roughly $10.6B-$15.8B (using IBM's per-record cost); some scaled estimates ran far higher. Progress Software's own direct costs not fully disclosed; it faced an SEC investigation and dozens of class-action lawsuits (40M+ claimants).
example_incidents.ransom_demanded_or_paid: Clop did not encrypt systems; it demanded extortion payments from individual victim organizations (amounts varied and were not publicly itemized). Many victims declined to pay.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: This was a data-theft (not encryption) event, so impact was breach-remediation and notification rather than operational downtime; remediation and victim-notification stretched over many months into 2024.
example_incidents.data_impact: Over 2,700 organizations confirmed impacted and approximately 93.3 million individuals' personal data exposed (estimates ranged 64M-95M+ over time).

example_incidents.summary: BlackSuit ransomware crippled CDK Global's Dealer Management System SaaS, which powers operations for ~15,000 auto dealerships across the U.S. and Canada; a second intrusion during recovery on June 19 prolonged the outage.
example_incidents.financial_impact: Anderson Economic Group estimated total dealer losses exceeding $1 billion (revised up from ~$944M) from roughly two-plus weeks of disruption.
example_incidents.ransom_demanded_or_paid: BlackSuit initially demanded ~$10M, reportedly escalating toward $50M+. CDK is widely reported to have paid approximately $25 million in Bitcoin (wallets tied to BlackSuit received ~$25M about two days after the attack, per CyberScoop).
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: Dealerships reverted to manual/pen-and-paper processes for nearly two weeks; CDK announced services restored for nearly all dealerships by around July 4, 2024.
example_incidents.data_impact: Primarily operational outage; extent of any data exfiltration less publicly quantified than the operational and financial disruption.

example_incidents.summary: SafePay ransomware caused a global outage at Ingram Micro, one of the world's largest IT distributors; intrusion is attributed to compromised credentials on the Palo Alto GlobalProtect VPN, halting worldwide order processing.
example_incidents.financial_impact: Specific revenue loss not publicly disclosed; multi-day global halt of order processing at a distributor with ~$48B annual revenue implies material lost/delayed transactions, though the company did not quantify it publicly.
example_incidents.ransom_demanded_or_paid: Ransom amount not publicly disclosed; on July 29-30, 2025 SafePay threatened to leak ~3.5TB of allegedly stolen data unless paid. No confirmation of payment.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: Systems failed around 8:00 AM ET on July 3; website and staged order processing resumed July 7-8; the company reported operations back to normal worldwide by July 9, 2025.
example_incidents.data_impact: Reported exposure of personal data of over 42,000 employees and applicants; SafePay claimed ~3.5TB of data.

example_incidents.summary: After Quanta (a major Apple ODM) declined to pay, REvil pivoted to extort Apple directly, publishing stolen schematics for unreleased products, timed to Apple's 'Spring Loaded' launch event — a landmark IP-theft extortion in the tech hardware supply chain.
example_incidents.financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed. Impact was primarily reputational and IP-confidentiality loss (leaked device blueprints) rather than reported revenue loss.
example_incidents.ransom_demanded_or_paid: REvil demanded $50 million, reportedly escalating toward $100M; the ransom was not paid by Quanta (and REvil eventually removed the leaked files). No confirmed payment.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: Operational downtime not the primary reported impact; this was chiefly a data-exfiltration/IP-leak extortion event.
example_incidents.data_impact: Theft and partial publication of confidential design schematics/blueprints for unreleased Apple devices (MacBook, Apple Watch drawings).

example_incidents.summary: Clop ransomware struck German enterprise-software giant Software AG, encrypting internal systems and stealing about 1TB of data, then publishing files after the company refused to negotiate — an early high-profile double-extortion case in the software industry.
example_incidents.financial_impact: Direct financial loss not fully disclosed; the company reported internal-network disruption but said customer-facing cloud services were unaffected.
example_incidents.ransom_demanded_or_paid: Clop demanded approximately $23 million. Software AG refused to pay.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: Internal network, help desk and some internal communications were disrupted for a period in October 2020; customer cloud services remained operational.
example_incidents.data_impact: About 1TB of data stolen, including employee passport/ID data, health-related documents and internal emails; screenshots and files leaked publicly after negotiations broke down.

example_incidents.summary: Hunters International claimed a January 2025 ransomware attack on Tata Technologies (engineering/IT-services arm of the Tata group), later leaking 1.4TB of stolen data; Tata Motors disclosed a ransomware incident to Indian stock exchanges.
example_incidents.financial_impact: Not publicly disclosed; the company said client-delivery services remained unaffected. No quantified revenue loss reported.
example_incidents.ransom_demanded_or_paid: Specific ransom amount not disclosed; Hunters International threatened public release of the data and, when unpaid, leaked it (~730,000 files) on its dark-web site in March 2025.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: Temporary disruption to some IT services per the January stock-exchange disclosure; client delivery reported unaffected. Detailed recovery timeline not publicly quantified.
example_incidents.data_impact: Claimed theft of 1.4TB (~730,000 files) including current/former employee personal details, purchase orders and confidential customer contracts (India and U.S. customers).

example_incidents.summary: On January 20, 2023, QuickLogic Corporation detected a ransomware infection affecting a limited number of IT systems. The Company promptly began an assessment, notified law enforcement, and engaged cybersecurity professionals to investigate the incident.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: The Company has continued its business operations during this incident and successfully restored all of its critical operational data.

example_incidents.summary: On April 17, 2023, NCR Corporation announced that a single data center outage affecting some functionality for its commerce customers was caused by a cyber ransomware incident. The company is assessing the impact of the incident on its operations and financial results.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: On February 23, 2023, DISH Network Corporation announced a network outage due to a cyber-security incident. Following the incident, it was determined that certain data was extracted from the Corporation's IT systems, potentially including personal information, prompting an ongoing investigation.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: The Corporation's internal communications, customer call centers, and internet sites have been affected, but DISH, Sling, and their wireless and data networks remain operational. The Corporation is actively engaged in restoring the affected systems and is making steady progress.
example_incidents.data_impact: It is possible that the extracted data includes personal information.

example_incidents.summary: NCR Voyix Corporation experienced a ransomware incident in April 2023, which impacted its business operations. The company has since been working on efforts to prevent or mitigate such incidents in the future.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: AFG Companies, Inc. is facing a lawsuit from Brand Engagement Network Inc. (BEN) for allegedly concealing a ransomware attack on their network prior to an agreement signed in August 2023. The lawsuit claims that this concealment hindered BEN's ability to deliver AI solutions to automotive dealerships, causing significant delays and damaging trust in the partnership.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Rackspace Technology experienced a ransomware attack at the end of 2022, which was highly publicized and resulted in a loss of approximately $30 million in high-margin revenue. The company has since implemented a strategy to transform its business and mitigate the impact of the attack.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Ingram Micro identified ransomware on certain internal systems and took steps to secure the environment, including taking systems offline. The Company is investigating the incident with cybersecurity experts and has notified law enforcement.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: The Company is working diligently to restore the affected systems to process and ship orders.

example_incidents.summary: Data I/O Corporation reported a ransomware incident that was identified on August 16, 2025. The attack was not targeted and originated from a vulnerability in a third-party firewall service. The company has restored all systems and believes there was no revenue loss due to the incident.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: All systems operational with no impact to customers or orders; incident contained and remediated.

example_incidents.summary: On March 11, 2026, Trio-Tech International's subsidiary in Singapore experienced a ransomware incident that resulted in the encryption of certain files. The incident escalated on March 18, leading to the unauthorized disclosure of company data, prompting the company to activate response protocols and notify law enforcement.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: The subsidiary took its network offline and is in the process of restoring affected systems.
example_incidents.data_impact: The scope of the data potentially affected has not yet been fully determined.

example_incidents.summary: Brand Engagement Network Inc. reported a ransomware attack on its network shortly before the termination of an Exclusive Reseller Agreement with AFG Companies, Inc. The company has filed a lawsuit against AFG alleging fraudulent misrepresentation and breach of contract related to the attack.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: CISA has confirmed that ransomware gangs are exploiting vulnerabilities in SonicWall's SMA1000 appliances. The vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410, have been linked to the deployment of custom malware by a threat actor identified as UTA0533.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: The Qilin ransomware gang exploited a critical vulnerability in Palo Alto Networks' GlobalProtect VPN to breach networks and deploy ransomware. Multiple distinct intrusions were reported in June 2026, leading to domain-wide encryption and suggesting ongoing exploitation of the flaw.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: The JadePuffer threat actor has launched a ransomware attack targeting AI model data using a custom malware called EncForge. This ransomware specifically encrypts AI assets such as training datasets and model checkpoints, potentially costing organizations significant time and financial resources to recover.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: A new ransomware group called Spirals executed a corporate intrusion and encrypted an IT services firm's network in under 24 hours. The attack involved data theft and encryption, with threats of public exposure of stolen data unless a ransom was paid.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Karen Serobovich Vardanyan, a member of the Ryuk ransomware gang, pleaded guilty to hacking U.S. companies and deploying ransomware to encrypt their systems. He was involved in multiple attacks, including one on a Michigan company that paid 200 BTC, and is estimated to have contributed to around $15 million in ransom payments across various organizations.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: CISA has ordered U.S. government agencies to secure their Check Point Remote Access VPN and Mobile Access deployments against a critical vulnerability exploited in zero-day attacks by Qilin ransomware affiliates. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote attackers to bypass authentication and establish a VPN connection, affecting a few dozen organizations worldwide.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Trellix, an international cybersecurity firm, experienced a breach of its source code repository, claimed by the RansomHouse hackers. The threat actor leaked a small set of images as proof and indicated that data encryption occurred during the intrusion. Trellix is currently investigating the incident and has notified law enforcement.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: A critical flaw in cPanel, tracked as CVE-2026-41940, is being exploited in mass ransomware attacks by the Sorry ransomware group. The attacks have compromised at least 44,000 IP addresses running cPanel, encrypting files and demanding ransom payments from victims.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: The Interlock ransomware gang exploited a zero-day vulnerability in Cisco's Secure Firewall Management Center software, allowing remote code execution. Cisco patched the flaw on March 4, 2026, after it was exploited for over a month, impacting multiple organizations.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice charged Angelo Martino, a former employee of DigitalMint, for conspiracy related to his involvement with the BlackCat ransomware operation. Martino and accomplices were accused of demanding ransom payments while threatening to leak stolen data from victims' networks, with at least five U.S. organizations affected, including a nonprofit and a financial services firm that paid significant ransoms.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Marquis Software Solutions experienced a ransomware attack on August 14, 2025, after hackers breached its network via a compromised SonicWall firewall. The attackers stole files containing personal information from business partners, affecting operations at 74 U.S. banks and leading Marquis to file a lawsuit against SonicWall for negligence and misrepresentation.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Advantest Corporation, a Japanese tech giant, was targeted in a ransomware attack that may have affected customer or employee data. The company detected unusual activity in its IT environment on February 15 and is currently investigating the incident with the help of third-party cybersecurity specialists.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: SmarterTools confirmed a breach by the Warlock ransomware gang, which exploited a vulnerability in its SmarterMail software. Although the attackers gained access to the network, encryption of data was prevented by security measures, and the company restored data from backups.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: impacted systems were isolated, and data was restored from fresh backups
example_incidents.data_impact: 12 Windows servers compromised; customer data not directly impacted

example_incidents.summary: Hitachi Vantara experienced a ransomware attack attributed to the Akira group, leading to the company taking servers offline to contain the incident. The attack disrupted some systems, but customers with self-hosted environments could still access their data as usual.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: Hitachi Vantara took servers offline to contain the incident and is working with third-party experts to remediate the situation and bring systems back online.

example_incidents.summary: Two malicious VSCode Marketplace extensions were found deploying in-development ransomware, exposing gaps in Microsoft's review process. The extensions, which were downloaded a few times before removal, contained a PowerShell command that downloaded ransomware from a remote server, encrypting files in a specific folder and demanding payment in ShibaCoin for recovery.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: The Mora_001 ransomware group has been exploiting Fortinet vulnerabilities to deploy a custom ransomware strain called SuperBlack. The attacks involve gaining super admin privileges, stealing data, and encrypting files for double extortion, with evidence suggesting links to the LockBit ransomware operation.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Lee Enterprises was attacked by the Qilin ransomware gang on February 3, 2025, leading to significant operational disruptions and the encryption of critical applications. The attackers have threatened to leak 120,000 stolen files unless a ransom is paid by March 5, 2025.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: significant operational disruptions, losing access to internal systems and cloud storage, corporate VPNs not working
example_incidents.data_impact: 120,000 files totaling 350GB, including government ID scans, non-disclosure agreements, financial spreadsheets, contracts/agreements, and other confidential documents

example_incidents.summary: In late 2024, a China-based threat actor known as Emperor Dragonfly launched a ransomware attack against an Asian software and services company, deploying RA World ransomware and demanding a ransom of $2 million. This incident highlights the potential overlap between state-backed cyber espionage and financially motivated cybercrime, as the tools used were previously associated with espionage activities.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: In November 2024, a South Asian software company was targeted in a ransomware attack by the RA World group, which is linked to a China-based threat actor known as Emperor Dragonfly. The attackers demanded a ransom of $2 million after deploying the RA World ransomware, following a series of espionage activities in the region.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Tata Technologies Ltd. experienced a ransomware attack that temporarily affected some of its IT services. Despite the attack, client delivery services remained fully operational, and the company is currently investigating the incident with cybersecurity experts.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: Some IT services were suspended temporarily and have now been restored.

example_incidents.summary: Atos, a French government contractor, denied claims by the Space Bears ransomware gang that they compromised one of its databases. The group threatened to leak stolen data on their dark web site, but Atos stated there was no evidence of a breach affecting their systems and that they had received no ransom demand.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: In April 2024, threat actors exploited compromised credentials to access customer accounts on the Snowflake cloud data platform, exporting databases and extorting companies to prevent public release of the data. The attacks affected numerous organizations, including AT&T and TicketMaster, leading to significant data exposure and financial demands.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed
example_incidents.data_impact: hundreds of millions of individuals affected, including 109 million call logs from AT&T and 560 million customers from TicketMaster

example_incidents.summary: The Clop ransomware gang has claimed responsibility for data theft attacks against Cleo, utilizing zero-day vulnerabilities to breach corporate networks and steal data. The gang confirmed they are behind the exploitation of vulnerabilities CVE-2024-50623 and CVE-2024-55956, which allowed them to gain unauthorized access and install backdoors for further data theft.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Blue Yonder, a SaaS provider, was breached by the Termite ransomware gang in November 2023. The attackers claimed to have stolen 680GB of data and caused significant operational disruptions for Blue Yonder's customers, including major retailers. The company is currently investigating the claims and working to restore services for affected clients.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: Blue Yonder has since brought back online some of the impacted customers and is now working with external cybersecurity experts to help others return to normal business operations.
example_incidents.data_impact: 680GB of files including database dumps, email lists for future attacks (over 16000), documents (over 200000), reports, insurance documents.

example_incidents.summary: The Helldown ransomware operation exploits vulnerabilities in Zyxel firewalls to breach networks, steal data, and encrypt devices. As of November 7, 2024, Helldown listed 31 victims on its extortion portal, including Zyxel Europe, indicating a potential ransom payment by some victims.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: A critical vulnerability in Veeam Backup Replication software was exploited to deploy Frag ransomware, following similar attacks by Akira and Fog ransomware groups. The vulnerability allowed threat actors to gain remote code execution and access backup data, leading to the deployment of the Frag ransomware on compromised networks.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Young Consulting, a software solutions provider, suffered a ransomware attack by BlackSuit on April 10, 2024, leading to the exposure of sensitive data of 950,000 individuals. The company began notifying affected individuals about the breach and offered complimentary credit monitoring services after discovering the attack three days later when the attackers triggered encryption of their systems.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed
example_incidents.data_impact: 950,000 records; full names, Social Security numbers (SSNs), dates of birth, insurance claim information

example_incidents.summary: Young Consulting, a software solutions provider, was attacked by the BlackSuit ransomware on April 10, 2024, leading to the theft of sensitive data from approximately 950,000 individuals. The company began notifying affected individuals about the breach and offered complimentary credit monitoring services after discovering the attack three days later when the attackers triggered encryption of their systems.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed
example_incidents.data_impact: 950,000 records; full names, Social Security numbers (SSNs), dates of birth, insurance claim information

example_incidents.summary: The Mad Liberator gang targets AnyDesk users by using a fake Windows update screen to distract victims while exfiltrating data. They do not encrypt data but drop ransom notes, threatening to publish stolen files if their demands are not met.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: The SEC has concluded its investigation into Progress Software's handling of the MOVEit Transfer zero-day flaw that exposed data of over 95 million people. The Clop ransomware gang exploited this vulnerability to conduct a large-scale data theft campaign affecting numerous organizations worldwide.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed
example_incidents.data_impact: 95 million people affected, data types not specified

example_incidents.victim: Austal USA, Hoya, Integris Health, Fred Hutch Cancer Center
example_incidents.summary: The Hunters International ransomware group is targeting IT workers with a new malware called SharpRhino, which facilitates initial infection and privilege escalation. The group has been active in 2024, announcing 134 ransomware attacks against various organizations worldwide, including notable victims such as Austal USA and Hoya.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.group: Storm-0506, Storm-1175, Octo Tempest, Manatee Tempest
example_incidents.summary: CISA has warned that a VMware ESXi authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2024-37085) is being exploited in ransomware attacks by several gangs. These attackers gain admin privileges on hypervisors, steal sensitive data, and encrypt the file system, leading to significant operational disruptions.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: causing outages and disrupting business operations

example_incidents.summary: Play ransomware has developed a Linux version specifically targeting VMware ESXi virtual machines, marking a significant shift in their attack strategy. This ransomware not only encrypts files but also employs double-extortion tactics by stealing sensitive documents to pressure victims into paying. The FBI has reported that the group has breached approximately 300 organizations worldwide until October 2023.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: The BlackSuit ransomware gang claimed a cyberattack on KADOKAWA corporation, threatening to publish stolen data if a ransom is not paid. The attack, which occurred on June 8, has caused significant service outages across the company's operations, including its subsidiary Niconico.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: Most operations continue to be impacted, with all Niconico services still suspended. Accounting functions expected to be restored in early July.
example_incidents.data_impact: Contacts, confidential documents, employee data, business plans, and financial data.

example_incidents.summary: P2PInfect botnet has activated a ransomware module targeting Redis servers, encrypting files with specific extensions and appending '.encrypted' to them. The ransomware operates with limited privileges, primarily affecting configuration files due to Redis's in-memory deployment.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Yaroslav Vasinskyi, a member of the REvil ransomware group, was sentenced to 13 years in prison for his role in over 2,500 ransomware attacks, including the Kaseya supply-chain attack. The group engaged in double extortion, stealing corporate data and threatening to leak it if ransoms were not paid, demanding over $700 million in total. Vasinskyi was arrested in 2021 and extradited to the U.S. in 2022, where he pleaded guilty to multiple charges.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: In May 2023, the Philadelphia Inquirer experienced a security breach where attackers stole personal and financial information of over 25,000 individuals. The Cuba ransomware gang claimed responsibility for the attack, stating they had stolen various financial documents and threatened to leak them, although the newspaper disputed the authenticity of the leaked files.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: The attack disrupted the publication of the print newspaper, with home-delivery subscribers asked to catch up with the latest news using the newspaper's website, which remained unaffected.
example_incidents.data_impact: 25,549 individuals affected; personal and financial information including names, financial account numbers, credit/debit card numbers, security codes, access codes, passwords, or PINs.

example_incidents.summary: The HelloKitty ransomware operation has rebranded to HelloGookie and released sensitive data from previous attacks on CD Projekt Red and Cisco. This includes source code for popular games and internal Cisco information, alongside decryption keys for older ransomware victims.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed
example_incidents.data_impact: 450 GB of source code and internal information, including source code for Witcher 3, Gwent, Cyberpunk 2077, and Cisco network information

example_incidents.summary: The HelloKitty ransomware operation has rebranded to HelloGookie, releasing previously stolen data from CD Projekt Red and Cisco. This includes source code for popular games and internal information, along with decryption keys for older attacks. The threat actor claims to be the original creator of HelloKitty and has launched a new dark web portal for their operations.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed
example_incidents.data_impact: 450 GB of source code and internal information, including source code for Witcher 3, Gwent, Cyberpunk 2077, and various console SDKs

example_incidents.summary: Xplain, a Swiss technology provider, was attacked by the Play ransomware gang on May 23, 2023, leading to the leak of 65,000 sensitive government documents. The leaked data, which includes personal and classified information, was published on the darknet in early June 2023, prompting an investigation by the Swiss government.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed
example_incidents.data_impact: 65,000 government documents leaked, including personal data (names, email addresses, telephone numbers, and addresses), technical details, classified information, and account passwords
sources: National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) of Switzerland report

example_incidents.summary: Insomniac Games, a subsidiary of Sony, experienced a ransomware attack by the Rhysida group, resulting in the theft and online leak of personal information belonging to employees. After refusing to pay a $2 million ransom, the group leaked 1.67 TB of documents, including sensitive employment data and internal documents.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed
example_incidents.data_impact: over 1.3 million files, including personal information of employees, former employees, and independent contractors

example_incidents.summary: Blackbaud experienced a ransomware attack in May 2020, leading to a data breach that affected millions of individuals. The company paid a ransom of 24 Bitcoin after the attackers threatened to leak the stolen data, which included sensitive personal information from over 13,000 customers.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed
example_incidents.data_impact: over 13,000 Blackbaud business customers and their clients, including banking information, social security numbers, and plaintext credentials

example_incidents.summary: Tietoevry, a Finnish IT services company, suffered an Akira ransomware attack that impacted one of its data centers in Sweden, causing outages for multiple customers including Filmstaden and various universities and government agencies. The attack encrypted virtualization and management servers, leading to significant disruptions in services.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: The company is in the process of restoring infrastructure and services, but customers remain impacted as servers are brought back online.

example_incidents.summary: Xerox Business Solutions (XBS) suffered a ransomware attack claimed by the INC Ransomware group. The attack resulted in a limited amount of personal information being potentially exposed, according to Xerox Corporation's statement.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed
example_incidents.data_impact: limited amount of personal information possibly exposed

example_incidents.summary: HTC Global Services confirmed a cyberattack after the ALPHV ransomware gang leaked screenshots of stolen data online. The leaked data includes sensitive information such as passports, contact lists, emails, and confidential documents. The company is investigating the incident and has engaged cybersecurity experts to address the situation.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Cactus ransomware has been exploiting critical vulnerabilities in the Qlik Sense data analytics solution to breach networks. The attackers deploy the ransomware after gaining access through these vulnerabilities, utilizing various tools to maintain persistence and exfiltrate data.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Black Basta ransomware, a Russian-linked group, has extorted at least $107 million from over 90 victims since its emergence in April 2022. The group employs double-extortion tactics, stealing sensitive data before encrypting systems and threatening to publish the data if ransoms are not paid. Notable victims include the American Dental Association and Capita, among others.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed
sources: Department of Health and Human Services

example_incidents.summary: The ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware gang filed a complaint with the U.S. SEC against MeridianLink for not disclosing a cyberattack that allegedly impacted customer data. The gang claims to have stolen data from MeridianLink's network without encrypting it and threatened to leak the data unless a ransom is paid within 24 hours.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: minimal business interruption

example_incidents.summary: Threat actors exploited a zero-day vulnerability in SysAid's IT service management software to deploy Clop ransomware and exfiltrate data. The vulnerability, identified as CVE-2023-47246, allowed unauthorized code execution, leading to the installation of additional malware and data theft.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Attackers exploited a critical vulnerability in Atlassian Confluence to deploy Cerber ransomware, encrypting victims' files. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2023-22518, was actively targeted following the release of a proof-of-concept exploit, leading to multiple attacks against exposed Confluence servers.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Sony Interactive Entertainment experienced a data breach impacting approximately 6,800 individuals due to a zero-day vulnerability in the MOVEit Transfer platform. The Clop ransomware gang exploited this vulnerability, leading to the unauthorized download of sensitive information. Sony has since notified affected individuals and is offering credit monitoring services.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: The platform was taken offline on June 2, 2023, and the vulnerability was remediated.
sources: Office of the Maine Attorney General

example_incidents.summary: Hackers exploited a vulnerability in Openfire messaging servers to encrypt files with ransomware, appending the .locked1 extension. Reports indicate that multiple Openfire servers were affected, with ransom demands typically between .09 to .12 bitcoins.
example_incidents.ransom_demanded_or_paid: ransom demands ranging from .09 to .12 bitcoins
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: The BlackCat ransomware gang utilized a new Sphynx encryptor to breach Sophos, encrypting 39 Azure Storage accounts after gaining access through stolen credentials. The attackers employed various tools and techniques to infiltrate the victim's systems, leading to significant data encryption and potential exposure.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: LogicMonitor confirmed that some users of its SaaS platform were victims of ransomware attacks. Anonymous sources indicated that threat actors hacked customer accounts and deployed ransomware using the platform's on-premise Collector sensors. The company is working with affected customers to mitigate the impact of the attacks.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: LogicMonitor is currently working on restoring time-series data for trial/demo customer portals located in the US-WEST region. Trial/demo customer portals in the EU-WEST and US-EAST region that were impacted earlier have now been restored and are fully accessible.

example_incidents.summary: Citrix NetScaler systems have been compromised by a threat actor linked to the FIN8 hacking group, exploiting a critical remote code execution flaw (CVE-2023-3519). Sophos reports that the campaign involves payload injections and is assessed to be part of a ransomware attack chain, with evidence of numerous webshells deployed across compromised servers.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: CloudNordic and AzeroCloud, Danish hosting providers, suffered a ransomware attack that resulted in the loss of most customer data and forced a complete shutdown of their systems. The firms have stated they will not pay the ransom and are working with security experts to assess the damage and recover data, but many customers have lost everything stored in the cloud.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: Systems shut down, recovery process ongoing but not smooth; some servers restored without data.
example_incidents.data_impact: Majority of customer data lost, affecting several hundred Danish companies.

example_incidents.summary: LolekHosted, a bulletproof hosting provider, was seized by law enforcement on August 8, 2023, for facilitating Netwalker ransomware attacks. Five administrators were arrested, and the service was used by cybercriminals to execute approximately 50 ransomware attacks globally. The operation was part of a coordinated effort by the FBI, IRS, and Europol.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Ashley Liles, a former IT employee, was sentenced to over three years in prison for attempting to blackmail his employer during a ransomware attack. He impersonated the ransomware gang and tried to redirect the ransom payment to his own cryptocurrency wallet, but the company did not comply with the demands, leading to his arrest and conviction.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed
example_incidents.data_impact: accessed private emails of a board member over 300 times
sources: South East Regional Organised Crime Unit (SEROCU) press release

example_incidents.summary: The LockBit ransomware gang demanded $70 million from TSMC, claiming to have stolen sensitive data. TSMC denied being hacked, stating that the breach occurred at one of its IT hardware suppliers, Kinmax Technology, which experienced a cybersecurity incident leading to data exfiltration.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: The Clop ransomware gang has claimed responsibility for the MOVEit Transfer data-theft attacks, exploiting a zero-day vulnerability to breach servers of hundreds of companies. Zellis, a UK payroll and HR solutions provider, confirmed it suffered a data breach due to these attacks, impacting some of its customers, while Aer Lingus and British Airways also reported being affected.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: disconnected the server that utilizes MOVEit software and engaged an expert external security incident response team

example_incidents.summary: L3Harris, a defense company, was targeted by a ransomware operation named Abyss. The attack has drawn attention due to the company's significant size and the nature of the threat posed by the ransomware group.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Dish Network experienced a ransomware attack on February 23, 2023, which likely resulted in the payment of a ransom based on the company's communications. The attack compromised confidential records and sensitive information of current and former employees, but customer data was not affected. The incident has led to multiple class-action lawsuits against the company for alleged cybersecurity failures.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: massive outage that affected its websites and apps
example_incidents.data_impact: 296,851 individuals affected; exposed information includes names, personal identifiers, driver's license numbers, health insurance information, and COVID-19 vaccination status

example_incidents.summary: MalasLocker ransomware targets Zimbra servers, encrypting emails and demanding donations to a charity instead of traditional ransom payments. The operation began in March 2023, with victims reporting encrypted files and unusual ransom notes requesting proof of charity donations for decryption.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed
example_incidents.data_impact: 169 Zimbra configurations and data from three companies

example_incidents.summary: ScanSource, a U.S.-based technology provider, confirmed it suffered a ransomware attack on May 14, 2023, impacting its systems and customer portals. The attack has caused significant operational disruptions, with delays expected in service provision to customers in North America and Brazil.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: The company is working diligently to bring affected systems back online, while also mitigating the impact on its business.

example_incidents.summary: Constellation Software confirmed a ransomware attack by the ALPHV gang, which involved the theft of over 1 TB of confidential data. The company stated that the incident was limited to a small number of systems and that they have restored the affected IT infrastructure. Business partners and individuals whose information was stolen are being contacted with further details.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: The company contained the attack and has restored all impacted IT infrastructure systems.
example_incidents.data_impact: A limited amount of personal information of individuals and business partner data was impacted.

example_incidents.summary: Yellow Pages Canada has confirmed that it suffered a cyber attack attributed to the Black Basta ransomware group. The attack resulted in the leakage of data, although specific details about the data affected have not been disclosed.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Microsoft has attributed recent attacks on PaperCut servers to the Clop and LockBit ransomware operations, which exploited vulnerabilities to steal corporate data. The Clop gang confirmed their involvement, stating they used the vulnerabilities for initial access rather than directly stealing documents from the server.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Yellow Pages Canada confirmed a cyber attack by the Black Basta ransomware group, which leaked sensitive customer and employee data. The attack is believed to have occurred on or after March 15, 2023, and the company is notifying impacted individuals and reporting to privacy authorities.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: Substantially all of our services have now been restored.
example_incidents.data_impact: sensitive documents including ID documents, tax documents, sales and purchase agreements, and financial spreadsheets

example_incidents.summary: Fortra reported that the Clop ransomware gang exploited a zero-day vulnerability in the GoAnywhere MFT solution to steal data from over 130 companies. The exploitation occurred between January 18 and January 30, 2023, leading to unauthorized access and data breaches.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Action1 RMM software is being abused by threat actors in ransomware attacks, allowing them to gain persistence and execute commands on compromised networks. The software has been linked to multiple ransomware incidents, with tactics resembling those of the Monti group, which exploited the Log4Shell vulnerability.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: MSI confirmed a security breach following claims of a ransomware attack by the Money Message gang, which has threatened to leak stolen files unless a ransom of $4 million is paid. The company reported that some of its information service systems were affected but stated that there has been no significant operational or financial impact.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: MSI's IT department has initiated information security defense mechanism and recovery procedures.
example_incidents.data_impact: approximately 1.5TB of documents, including ERP databases, software source code, private keys, and BIOS firmware

example_incidents.summary: Clop ransomware claims to have breached over 130 organizations by exploiting a zero-day vulnerability in the GoAnywhere MFT secure file transfer tool. They allegedly stole data but did not deploy ransomware, opting instead to extort their victims by threatening to leak the stolen documents.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: temporary service outage; service continues to be restored on a customer-by-customer basis

example_incidents.summary: VMware has issued a warning regarding a large-scale ransomware campaign targeting unpatched ESXi servers, specifically exploiting the OpenSLP service. The ransomware, known as ESXiArgs, encrypts various file types on compromised servers, affecting thousands of targets worldwide.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed
example_incidents.data_impact: over 2,400 servers affected; .vmxf, .vmx, .vmdk, .vmsd, and .nvra files encrypted

example_incidents.summary: A massive ransomware attack targeting VMware ESXi servers has been reported, exploiting a known vulnerability (CVE-2021-21974). Approximately 2,400 devices were compromised, with only four ransom payments totaling $88,000 made, likely due to available recovery resources for affected admins.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Avast has released a free decryptor for the BianLian ransomware strain, allowing victims to recover locked files without paying the hackers. The decryptor is designed to assist those affected by known variants of the ransomware, which encrypts files and threatens to publish private data if demands are not met.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: A ransomware attack on Heilbronn Stimme disrupted the printing systems of the newspaper and its parent media group, Stimme Mediengruppe. The attack led to the publication of an emergency six-page edition and the lifting of the paywall on their website due to circulation issues. The media group is collaborating with police and cybersecurity experts to resolve the situation.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: Printing systems were crippled, leading to emergency editions being printed via a third party. Communication via phone and email was offline during the weekend.

example_incidents.victim: QNAP and Asustor NAS device users
example_incidents.summary: The Dutch National Police, in collaboration with Responders.NU, successfully tricked the DeadBolt ransomware gang into providing 155 decryption keys by faking ransom payments. This operation allowed victims of the DeadBolt ransomware to recover their files without incurring costs, as the police managed to cancel the transactions before they were confirmed on the Bitcoin blockchain.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.victim: QNAP and Asustor Network Attached Storage (NAS) device users
example_incidents.summary: The Dutch National Police, in collaboration with Responders.NU, successfully tricked the DeadBolt ransomware gang into providing 155 decryption keys by faking ransom payments. This operation allowed victims of the DeadBolt ransomware to recover their files without incurring costs, as the police managed to cancel the transactions before they were confirmed on the Bitcoin blockchain.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Microsoft Exchange servers were hacked to deploy LockBit ransomware, utilizing a previously deployed web shell to escalate privileges and encrypt network systems. The attackers stole approximately 1.3 TB of data within a week of gaining access to the Active Directory admin account.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: ADATA denies a recent cyberattack by RansomHouse, asserting that the leaked data is from a 2021 breach. RansomHouse claims to have stolen 1TB of documents in a 2022 attack, but ADATA states that no successful attacks have occurred since their 2021 incident.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed
example_incidents.data_impact: 1TB of documents claimed stolen, originally from a May 2021 RagnarLocker ransomware attack

example_incidents.summary: TargetCompany has been targeted by the FARGO ransomware, which specifically focuses on Microsoft SQL servers. The ransomware encrypts files and threatens to leak stolen data unless a ransom is paid, exploiting vulnerabilities and weak credentials in database management systems.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: QNAP Systems, Inc. is facing ongoing DeadBolt ransomware attacks that exploit a zero-day vulnerability in Photo Station. The company has released patches to address the security flaw, but attacks continue to affect NAS devices directly connected to the Internet.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Baker & Taylor, a leading library services firm, confirmed it was hit by a ransomware attack that disrupted its business-critical systems. The company is actively working to restore its systems after the attack, which occurred over the weekend prior to August 23, 2022.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: Systems were down for more than a week as technical teams worked on restoring impacted servers.

example_incidents.summary: Entrust suffered a data breach on June 18, where LockBit ransomware gang stole data and threatened to leak it. Although Entrust did not pay the ransom, LockBit announced plans to publish the stolen data, which they later did on August 27, despite facing a DDoS attack that temporarily hindered their operations.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Bandai Namco confirmed a cyberattack on July 3, 2022, which may have resulted in the theft of customer personal data. The BlackCat ransomware group claimed responsibility for the breach, indicating that corporate data was stolen during the attack.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: QNAP has warned customers about a new ransomware strain called Checkmate that targets NAS devices. The ransomware encrypts files and demands a ransom of $15,000 in bitcoins for decryption. The attacks exploit weak passwords and SMB services exposed to the internet, prompting QNAP to advise users to secure their devices and use strong passwords.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Macmillan, a publishing giant, was forced to shut down their network and offices due to a likely ransomware attack. The incident appears to be linked to the LockBit ransomware group, which has been active in targeting various organizations.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: forced to shut down their network and offices while recovering from a security incident
sources: The Week in Ransomware - July 1st 2022 - Bug Bounties

example_incidents.summary: AvosLocker and Cerber2021 ransomware gangs are exploiting a recently patched vulnerability in Atlassian Confluence servers to gain unauthorized access and deploy ransomware. Multiple organizations worldwide have been targeted, leading to significant security concerns and calls for immediate patching of the affected systems.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: LockBit ransomware gang claimed to have hacked Mandiant and stolen 356,841 files, threatening to leak them online. Mandiant stated there is no evidence supporting these claims and is investigating the situation.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed
example_incidents.data_impact: 356,841 files claimed to be stolen, specific data types not disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Nikkei's Singapore branch suffered a ransomware attack on May 13, 2022, attributed to the Conti ransomware gang. This incident is part of a broader trend of ransomware attacks affecting various organizations globally.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: not publicly disclosed

example_incidents.summary: Nikkei's Asian unit was hit by a ransomware attack on May 13, 2022, prompting an internal investigation. The company shut down the affected server and is currently assessing the nature and scope of the attack, including whether customer data was accessed.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: Nikkei Group Asia immediately shut down the affected server and took other measures to minimize the impact.
example_incidents.data_impact: The affected server likely contained customer data, but no evidence of a data leak has been found so far.

example_incidents.summary: Onleihe, an online library app, faced issues after a cyberattack targeted its service provider EKZ on April 18, 2022. The attack led to system failures and data leaks, with LockBit 2.0 claiming responsibility. The incident affected various media formats, causing streaming errors and incomplete e-book files for users.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: Most systems have been restored, but invoice issuing and order processing are still impacted by delays.

example_incidents.summary: Onleihe faced significant issues after a cyberattack on its service provider EKZ, which occurred on April 18, 2022. The attack led to system failures that affected the lending of various media formats, including eBooks, audiobooks, and videos, with many files requiring re-encryption and re-uploading. The LockBit 2.0 group claimed responsibility for the attack and subsequently leaked data allegedly stolen from EKZ.
example_incidents.downtime_and_recovery: Most systems have been restored, but invoice issuing and order processing are still impacted by delays.

data_source_notes: STEP 1 (base data): The endpoint given in the task, https://api.ransomware.live/v2/victims/sector/Technology, is incorrect on the current API (v6.0 backend) — it 302-redirects to the API docs page. The correct free endpoint is https://api.ransomware.live/v2/sectorvictims/Technology (confirmed via the ransomware.live/apidocs swagger listing). Direct curl to the API repeatedly failed with connection code 000 after the first call, consistent with aggressive per-IP rate limiting/blocking; I could not reliably pull the raw JSON via curl. WebFetch on the correct /v2/sectorvictims/Technology endpoint DID return data (the fast-model summary reported 100+ victim records and surfaced notable names incl. Synopsys, ARM Holdings, Indra, Mercado Libre, and various 2026-dated entries). Caveat: the API list appears to blend in infostealer/HudsonRock enrichment fields (per-user counts), and many entries are very recent (2026) and hard to independently verify, so for the notable-incident selection I deliberately relied on well-documented, independently corroborated incidents rather than unverifiable API rows. STEP 2 (supplemental): ransomlook.io was not successfully retrieved. https://ransomwhat.telemetry.ltd/posts.json 302-redirected to https://ransomwatch.telemetry.ltd/ (host changed); I did not chase the redirect further as the primary and news sources already provided sufficient corroboration. Neither supplemental source materially contributed; note them as attempted/partially-failed. STEP 3-5: All example-incident details and aggregate statistics were gathered via WebSearch against primary news outlets, vendor threat reports and official reports, with sources cited per incident and per statistic. No figures were fabricated; where a specific figure (e.g., exact revenue loss for Ingram Micro or Tata Technologies) was not publicly reported, that is stated explicitly. Note: NTT Communications (Feb 2025, 17,891 orgs) was considered for geographic diversity but excluded from example_incidents because it was an unauthorized-access data breach not claimed by a ransomware group; it is referenced only illustratively in the exposure taxonomy.

data_source_notes:
STEP 1 (primary source): The literal endpoint given in the task, https://api.ransomware.live/v2/victims/sector/Manufacturing, returned an HTTP 302 redirect to /apidocs/ (that path no longer exists on the current v6.0-beta "Aegis" site). I fetched the live API docs page (https://www.ransomware.live/apidocs) and found the correct current endpoint is /v2/sectorvictims/<sector>. I successfully pulled https://api.ransomware.live/v2/sectorvictims/Manufacturing (HTTP 200, ~4.0MB JSON payload, no rate-limit/429 encountered) and parsed all 4,434 victim records client-side (via PowerShell/Invoke-WebRequest and curl.exe, since the WebFetch tool's own agent could not render/return the raw 4MB JSON body directly). This was used to derive group/country/year distribution stats and to identify well-known victim names for Step 3. Note: WebFetch itself could not be used directly on the API (it auto-followed the 302 to the marketing docs page rather than returning raw JSON), so Bash/PowerShell HTTP calls were used as a fallback per the task's rate-limit contingency guidance.

STEP 2 (supplemental corroboration): www.ransomlook.io/api/search?query=Manufacturing returned HTTP 400 Bad Request (endpoint/query format likely changed or requires different parameters) — could not be used. ransomwhat.telemetry.ltd/posts.json redirected to ransomwatch.telemetry.ltd, which now shows only a notice that the RansomWatch project is archived/no longer maintained, with no queryable post data — could not be used. Neither supplemental source yielded usable data; all corroboration for the notable incidents (Step 3) instead came from WebSearch across mainstream security-news outlets (BleepingComputer, SecurityWeek, SecurityAffairs, TechCrunch, Dark Reading, Industrial Cyber, CPO Magazine, etc.), which is consistent with the task's fallback instruction.

STEP 3: All 8 example incidents were cross-checked as present in the ransomware.live Manufacturing dataset pull (matched by victim/domain name, group, and approximate date) and then enriched with real reported financial/operational details via WebSearch. No numbers were fabricated; where a detail was not found in public reporting it is explicitly marked "not publicly disclosed."

STEP 5: Aggregate stats drawn from Sophos "State of Ransomware in Manufacturing and Production 2025" (industry-specific report, published Dec 2025), Coveware Quarterly Ransomware Reports (Q3/Q4 2025), IBM Cost of a Data Breach Report (industrial sector analysis, 2024/2025), and one industry-tracker roundup (Industrial Cyber) aggregating a separate 2025 ransomware-attack-volume report. No rate-limiting encountered on any WebSearch call.
